advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no real/malformed Jira link entry can carry both inwardIssue and outwardIssue keys, or document that map_remote_links intentionally records only the outward-priority key (a slight narrowing of the old direction-agnostic dedup).
evidence: Old code added both sides: `for side_key in ("inwardIssue", "outwardIssue"): ... existing.add((type_name, side_key_val))`

New code uses resolve_inbound_link which is outward-priority: link_direction.py:43-46 `if isinstance(outward, dict) and outward.get("key"): return outward["key"], base` then `if isinstance(inward, dict) ...`
backend.py:230 `other_key, relation = resolve_inbound_link(link)` — only one key returned; the fallback scan at 235-239 fires only when other_key is None.
advisory.finding: The PR claims map_remote_links absorbs _existing_jira_links dedup 'byte-identical', but the old _existing_jira_links iterated BOTH inwardIssue and outwardIssue keys of each link (adding an entry per keyed side), whereas map_remote_links delegates key selection to resolve_inbound_link, which returns only ONE key (outward takes priority over inward). A single link entry carrying BOTH inward and outward keys would record both (type,inward_key) and (type,outward_key) under the old code but only the outward key under the new code — a narrow divergence from the stated exact-preservation invariant.

advisory.finding: map_remote_links's unmapped-vendor-type contract (returns a (None, remote_key, vendor_type) entry so core never treats an uncanonicalizable link as absent) is never directly asserted. The only direct map_remote_links test covers a mapped 'Blocks' link; the unknown-type ADD test would pass whether map_remote_links surfaces a relation=None entry or omits the link entirely, so the anti-clobber guarantee is untested.
scenarios: A future refactor drops the lines 231-241 fallback key-scan; the unmapped link vanishes from the canonical set; the ADD dedup test still passes, so the regression ships undetected

evidence: outbound_links.py:154-158 — `for relation, other_key, opaque_vendor_type in canonical: if relation is None: continue  # ... never managed by us — left for inbound ADOPT`
test_link_removal_sync.py:159-168 — `test_unmanaged_jira_link_is_not_removed` uses `_BLOCKS_LINK` (a MAPPED type) with empty managed_refs, testing the managed-ref gate, not the relation=None gate

advisory.finding: The REMOVE pass's new `relation is None` skip guard — a MANAGED, locally-absent link of an UNMAPPED remote vendor type must NOT be removed — has no test. test_unmanaged_jira_link_is_not_removed exercises a mapped (Blocks) link that was never managed, not an unmapped-type link. If the None-guard at outbound_links.py:157 were removed, an unmapped link would reach should_propagate_removal with relation=None and could be wrongly clobbered.
scenarios: A human-added Jira link of a vendor type rebar cannot canonicalize is present remotely and absent locally; if the relation=None guard regresses, rebar could emit a REMOVE for a link it never managed and cannot map
